body:
Byte-level findings from #5363: Starfield.esm ships **181 `WTHS` records** (the SF replacement for WTHR) — each is just `EDID` + a ~2.5 KB `REFL` payload. The REFL blob is SF's BGS parameter serialization: a `BETH` container magic wrapping named parameters (`BGSWeatherSettingsForm`, `pParent`, `pDisplayNameK`, …). 26 of the 47 CLMTs reference only WTHS weathers through their `WSLT` seasonal table (Akila: 7 rows — Clear/PartlyCloudy/Cloudy/Fog/Rain, chances summing to 100).

Sample: `WTHS 0031FC4C WeatherUniqueAkila_Clear_C0_Unique`, REFL begins `… R F D P / R D I F / BETH / STRT / BGSWeatherSettingsForm…` — strings are visible in the blob (e.g. tail `…r_C0_Unique\0` from the EDID overlap).

Decoding this needs the xEdit SF1 `wbDefinitionsSF1.pas` WTHS layout (check the local reference library first per the repo's convention) — the parameter-block reader is a new subsystem. Until then `ClimateRecord::seasonal_weathers` holds the WSLT rows and exteriors on WTHS-only climates use the authored `DefaultWeather` WTHR (#5363's fix).
title: Decode Starfield WTHS weather records (EDID + REFL BGS parameter blob) — the real SF weather schema
